item.title: [Due in 3 days] Third-party telephony provider configuration opens on 30 October, with Soprano and Telesign first
item.description:
Any tenant still leaning on Microsoft-provided SMS or voice has one configuration window between 30 October and the February 2027 retirement.

Entra · deadline 2026-10-30 · Decide now whether the tenant migrates method or provider, and hold 30 October as the date configuration can begin.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Conditional Access policy plans (preview) are now documented: shared targeting and exclusions defined once, inherited by every rule, and a plan-level exclusion no rule can remove
item.description:
Sign-in logs will show plan rules as separate entries, and a plan-level exclusion silently applies to every rule; location-conditioned plans lose continuous access evaluation's instant IP enforcement during preview.

Entra · Before adopting plans, decide where emergency-access exclusions live, make sure sign-in log parsing and CA reporting handle rule entries, and keep location-based policies outside plans while the one-hour-token limitation applies.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [Due in 3 days] Entra makes Choose Your Own Telephony Provider generally available on 30 October; Microsoft-provided SMS and voice still retire 1 February 2027 (Global Administrators and external users 1 July 2027)
item.description:
A third party now sits in the MFA delivery path for every user it covers, and the 1 February 2027 retirement turns any account still relying only on SMS or voice into a blocking passkey prompt at sign-in.

Entra · deadline 2026-10-30 · Count the users whose only MFA method is SMS or voice, move them to passkeys or Authenticator before 1 February 2027, and buy a provider only for a documented residual population, with the provider treated as a tier-0 supplier.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [Due in 1 day] Reminder: the Microsoft-managed 'Require risk remediation for high-risk users' policy switches itself On the week of 28 October
item.description:
A tenant-wide CA policy that enforces itself is a change to sign-in behaviour nobody approved: high-risk users without a registered MFA method are blocked, and break-glass accounts are protected only if they are already excluded from the policy's group.

Entra · deadline 2026-10-28 · Open the Microsoft-managed policy in the Entra admin center now, confirm emergency-access accounts are excluded, compare its report-only results with your own risk policies, and set it On or Off deliberately before 28 October.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [Due in 7 days] Final reminder: the MemberOf rule operator stops processing on 3 November, and dynamic groups built on it freeze in their last state
item.description:
A group that stops recalculating does not fail loudly: it keeps whoever was in it on 3 November. A leaver stays in a group that grants access or a licence, a joiner never arrives in a group a Conditional Access policy targets, and an administrative unit stops following the population it was meant to scope. Nothing alerts, because nothing errors.

Entra · deadline 2026-11-03 · Query dynamic groups and administrative units for membership rules containing memberOf, list which Conditional Access policies, access packages and licence assignments target them, and replace each rule or convert the group to assigned membership before 3 November.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [Due in 1 day] A Microsoft-managed Conditional Access policy, Require risk remediation for high-risk users, starts in report-only mode and switches On the week of 28 October
item.description:
From the week of 28 October a policy the tenant did not write starts deciding sign-ins for high-risk users. Emergency access accounts are not excluded automatically, and a high-risk user without a registered MFA method cannot self-remediate and is blocked, which the help desk will see before the SOC does.

Entra · deadline 2026-10-28 · Find the Microsoft-managed policy in Conditional Access now (report-only since the week of 28 September), read its report-only results in the sign-in logs, exclude break-glass accounts, confirm the users it would touch can complete MFA, and decide before 28 October whether it turns On or is set to Off.

item.title: [New] MSRC discloses CVE-2026-97785, an elevation of privilege in Entra Application Proxy rated 10.0; Microsoft has fully mitigated it and customers have nothing to do
item.description:
Application Proxy publishes on-premises apps to the internet under Entra pre-authentication; a 10.0 authentication flaw there is worth recording against any unexplained App Proxy access before the mitigation date, which Microsoft does not state.

Entra · No patch. If you publish apps through Application Proxy, note the CVE in the risk register and check App Proxy sign-in and connector logs for anomalies you could not explain earlier.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Perception.Read.All and Perception.Manage.All enter Microsoft's permission file with 18 beta /security/agenticSecurity paths (playbooks, sessions, agent runs)
item.description:
Agentic Security sessions, agent runs, inputs and outputs are security-investigation content; a delegated grant of Perception.Manage.All lets an app start and cancel agent sessions as the user.

Graph · Add both names to the consent watch list and alert on a grant; nothing is grantable through Microsoft Graph yet, so there is no tenant action today.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] App management policies gain an audit state in Graph beta: evaluate credential and app restrictions without enforcing them
item.description:
An audit mode is how a tenant can measure what a 'no client secrets' or 'max credential lifetime' policy would break before switching it on, which is the usual reason those policies are never enforced.

Graph · Where app management policies are still off, plan an audit-state rollout of the credential restrictions and review what it reports; the value is beta-only.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Entra documents Microsoft-initiated revocation of compromised app credentials: tokenRevocations on applications and service principals, issuer 0e0fb671-b107-448b-a273-9d0ded7627a7
item.description:
A workload that suddenly fails with one of these AADSTS codes may be the first sign that Microsoft saw its secret or certificate in an attacker's hands; deleting the revocation to make the error go away re-opens the credential, and tokens already issued can keep working for up to 24 hours on some resources.

Entra · Add the five AADSTS codes and the initiator Azure Active Directory Protection Services on Update application / Update service principal to detections; treat a Microsoft-issued revocation as an incident, rotate the credential and remove anything the attacker added, and never delete the revocation as a fix.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Entra Agent ID: an agent identity blueprint can now be disabled in all tenants at once, and Microsoft warns agents in other tenants may fail
item.description:
An Agent ID Administrator in the publisher tenant can now switch off a blueprint's agents everywhere it was installed; that is a kill switch for a compromised agent and an outage lever if misused.

Entra · Add disabling a blueprint in all tenants to the agent incident runbook and watch Agent ID Administrator assignments, since that role can now reach agents in other tenants.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Microsoft Authenticator gets a new home page, account-restoration banner and guidance, and on Android a battery-optimization prompt; push and passwordless restore improves
item.description:
Help desks will see users asking about restore banners and a rating prompt that appears during sign-in; a user who has learned that Authenticator shows unexpected prompts is easier to talk into approving the wrong one.

Entra · Tell the service desk and update end-user screenshots; remind users that the rating prompt never asks for a number or an approval.

Entra · Add suspiciousCredentialAddition to the riskEventType lists your Sentinel and Defender rules match on, check that user-risk policies require remediation for it, and review the first detections against the AuditLogs 'User registered security info' events.

item.description:

Entra · Hunt for service principals with a non-null disabledByMicrosoftStatus, investigate their past consents and sign-ins, and route any re-enable request through the support process the page names.
